title_en: The Story of the Second Day of the Second Month
full_text_zh:
[P1] 二月二的故事
连环画出版社

[P2] 二月二的故事
司南/改编
杨景芝/绘画

从前，黄河边有一座龙斧山，山上有座龙王庙。山下住着小伙子强娃，他又勤劳又勇敢。

[P3] 强娃娶了采药姑娘
莹花。莹花姑娘又美丽
又善良。两个人在一起
十分幸福。
可是，这一带已经连
续三年大旱。穷人的日子
不好过，他们纷纷拜神求
雨，祈求老天爷开眼。

[P4] 强娃觉得光祈求老天爷没用，
他想去挖黑龙潭，挖出水来，大家
就有救了。
黑龙潭在不远的山口上，年景
好的时候，总是满满一潭清水，现在
呢，早干得见底了。强娃和莹花挖
啊，挖啊，足足忙了一个月，也没挖
出一滴水。

[P5] 二月初一这天，强娃像平时一样，卖力地挖着潭底的干泥巴。突然，一镢头下去金光四射！

就在这时，天上飞下个石头蛋蛋，在强娃和莹花脚边滚来滚去。

[P6] 哟，石头蛋蛋呼啦一下子变成了一只白鸽！莹花刚要捉它，它就扑棱棱飞了起来。

[P7] 强娃赶紧用手一挡，白鸽一下子跌在地上，变成了一个笑嘻嘻的老公公。
老公公对强娃和莹花说：“好孩子，感动天，希望还在龙斧山。龙斧山，劈山斧，一斧顶你一万五……”说完，老公公化作一缕青烟，不见了。
强娃和莹花按照老公公的指点，翻过三道山，越过两道岭，来到龙王庙。

[P8] 啊，眼前的铁架上放着
一把很大很大的斧头，看上去
足有千斤重。

强娃想：这就是老公公说的“劈
山斧”吧？他拿过斧头，扛在肩上。奇
怪！真轻！

[P9] 强娃和莹花连夜
赶回黑龙潭。天刚蒙
蒙亮，强娃就抡起劈
山斧，对准潭底的硬
盖，猛劈下去……

“轰隆隆……”大地开始
抖动，高山也摇晃起来，一股
清泉“咕嘟嘟”从黑龙潭里冒
出来了！

[P10] 泉水“哗哗”地流淌着，一片轻纱似的薄雾笼罩了黑龙潭。
接着，只听见一声雷响，一条青龙从潭水里抬起头来。
青龙长长地出了一口气，“呼啦”一声，腾空飞起。
这时候，天上乌云翻腾，雷声滚滚，豆大的雨点“噼里啪啦”直落下来，干旱的土地和枯萎的树木，终于喝足了雨水。

[P12] 雨停了，大家都跑来感谢强娃和莹花。这一天正好是二月初二。听，孩子们拍手唱着：“二月二，龙抬头，人不害病地丰收。”
从此，人们就说二月二是龙抬头的日子。

“二月二，龙抬头。”这个“龙抬头”不仅象征着春回大地，万物复苏，还代表着从这时候开始，每到黄昏，天上的“龙角星”就能出现在东方地平线上。中国古代历法的二十八宿中，东方七宿组成青龙形状，其中角宿一星与角宿二星，就是所谓的“龙角星”。
为迎接春耕季节的到来，这一天有许多仪式和禁忌。如中国北方旧俗，这天清晨起床，要用长竿敲打房梁，把龙唤醒，然后用草木灰向井台引一条“灰龙”，再用谷糠从井台到水缸引回一条“金龙”；有些地方是早早去河边打水，先得者当年必有好收成，去井台打水则称为“挑龙蛋”，但也有些地方不准打水，怕触动“龙头”。这一天，妇女不许动针，怕“伤龙眼”。有些地方用灶灰围绕房屋或村庄洒下一圈，表示挡邪避灾。人人理发，小孩子更要理发，称为“剃龙头”。

[P13] 二月二的吃食也多种多样。除了吃炒豆子外，还有吃年糕、猪头肉的，而面条则被称为“龙须”，饺子为“龙耳”，馄饨为“龙眼”，春饼为“龙鳞”。老北京吃春饼讲究“和菜”。金受申先生在《北京通》中说这词读作“火菜”，用各种素菜丝加肉丝、团粉拌炒而成，盖上一张“摊黄菜”即炒鸡蛋。其他配菜有酱肉、熏鸡等。春饼是用两个面剂儿合在一起擀成，烙熟再揭开，所以很薄，随后还要上锅蒸软，随吃随拿，卷着各种菜吃，吃起来十分适口。
关于二月二吃炒豆或者爆玉米花的习俗，还有个有趣的传说。一次玉帝降罪人间，命令三年不准下雨。司掌天河的玉龙不忍，便私自降雨，被玉帝打下天宫，压在大山下面，说是：“除非金豆开花，否则永不准回返天庭。”人们为了救这条玉龙，到处寻找开花的金豆，却无法找到。来年的二月初二，人们翻晒玉米种子，忽然发现它色泽金黄，正像金豆一般。于是家家户户炒豆、爆玉米花，向玉帝上供。玉龙也大声向玉帝喊道：“金豆开花 了！快放我出去！”玉帝无奈，只好赦免了玉龙。从此以后，人们每到二月二这天，就炒豆子、爆玉米花吃。
full_text_en:
[P1] The Story of the Second Day of the Second Month
Lianhuanhua Publishing House

[P2] The Story of the Second Day of the Second Month
Adapted by Si Nan
Illustrated by Yang Jingzhi

Long ago, by the Yellow River, there was a mountain called Longfu Mountain, with a Dragon King Temple on top. At the foot of the mountain lived a young man named Qiangwa, who was both hardworking and brave.

[P3] Qiangwa married the herb-gathering girl
Yinghua. Yinghua was beautiful
and kind. The two of them were
very happy together.
But this area had been suffering
from a three-year drought. The poor people's lives
were hard, so they all prayed to the gods for rain,
asking the old Heaven to open his eyes.

[P4] Qiangwa thought praying to the heavens was useless.
He wanted to dig up the Black Dragon Pond, to bring out water, and then everyone would be saved.
The Black Dragon Pond was on a nearby mountain pass. In good years, it was always full of clear water. But now, it had dried up to the bottom. Qiangwa and Yinghua dug and dug, working hard for a whole month, but they couldn't dig out a single drop of water.

[P5] On the first day of the second lunar month, Qiangwa, as usual, was digging hard at the dry mud at the bottom of the pond. Suddenly, a golden light burst forth from his shovel strike!

At that moment, a stone egg fell from the sky, rolling back and forth near Qiangwa and Yinghua's feet.

[P6] Oh, the stone egg suddenly turned into a white dove! Yinghua was about to catch it, but it flapped its wings and flew away.

[P7] Qiangwa quickly blocked with his hand, and the white dove fell to the ground, turning into an old man with a cheerful smile.
The old man said to Qiangwa and Yinghua, "Good children, you've moved heaven. Hope still lies in Longfu Mountain. Longfu Mountain, mountain-splitting axe, one axe stroke is worth 15,000..." After finishing, the old man turned into a wisp of blue smoke and disappeared.
Qiangwa and Yinghua followed the old man's instructions, crossed three mountains, passed over two ridges, and arrived at the Dragon King Temple.

[P8] Ah, on the iron rack in front of them was a huge, huge axe, looking as if it weighed a thousand jin.

Qiangwa thought: Could this be the 'Mountain-Splitting Axe' the old man mentioned? He picked up the axe and carried it on his shoulder. Strange! It was so light!

[P9] Qiangwa and Yinghua hurried back to the Black Dragon Pond overnight. Just as dawn broke, Qiangwa grabbed the mountain-splitting axe, aimed at the hard cover at the bottom of the pond, and swung down hard...

"Boom..." The earth began to tremble, the high mountains swayed, and a clear spring gushed out from the Black Dragon Pond with a "gurgle!"

[P10] The spring water flowed '哗哗' (hualua), and a thin mist like gauze covered the Black Dragon Pond.
Then, with a thunderclap, a green dragon raised its head from the pond water.
The green dragon let out a long breath, '呼啦' (hula), and soared into the sky.
At this moment, dark clouds swirled in the sky, thunder rolled, and large raindrops '噼里啪啦' (pilipala) fell straight down, finally quenching the thirsty land and withered trees.

[P12] The rain stopped, and everyone ran to thank Qiangwa and Yinghua. This day happened to be the second day of the second lunar month. Listen, the children are clapping and singing: 'February 2nd, the dragon raises its head, people stay healthy and the land yields a bountiful harvest.'
From then on, people said that February 2nd is the day the dragon raises its head.

'February 2nd, the dragon raises its head.' This 'dragon raising its head' not only symbolizes spring returning to the earth and all things reviving, but also signifies that from this time on, every evening, the 'Dragon Horn Star' appears on the eastern horizon. In ancient Chinese astronomy's Twenty-Eight Lunar Mansions, the seven mansions in the east form the shape of the Azure Dragon, among which the first and second stars of the Anger Mansion are known as the 'Dragon Horn Star'.
To welcome the arrival of the spring farming season, this day has many rituals and taboos. For example, in northern China's old customs, people would get up early in the morning, use a long pole to tap the roof beams to wake the dragon, then use wood ash to lead a 'gray dragon' to the well platform, and use bran to lead a 'golden dragon' back from the well platform to the water jar; in some places, people would go to the riverbank early to fetch water, and the first to do so would have a good harvest that year; fetching water from the well platform was called 'carrying the dragon egg,' but in some places, fetching water was forbidden, fearing it might disturb the 'dragon's head.' On this day, women were not allowed to sew, fearing they might 'hurt the dragon's eye.' In some places, people would sprinkle ash around houses or villages to ward off evil spirits. Everyone would get a haircut, and children especially would get their hair cut, called 'shaving the dragon's head.'

[P13] The food eaten on the second day of the second lunar month is also very diverse. Besides stir-fried beans, people also eat rice cakes and pork head meat. Noodles are called 'dragon's whiskers', dumplings are 'dragon's ears', wontons are 'dragon's eyes', and spring pancakes are 'dragon's scales'. In old Beijing, eating spring pancakes involves 'he cai' (mixed vegetables). Mr. Jin Shoushen mentioned in 'Beijing Tong' that this dish is pronounced 'huo cai', made by stir-frying various shredded vegetables with shredded meat and starch, then topped with a layer of 'tuan huang cai' (fried eggs). Other side dishes include braised meat and smoked chicken. Spring pancakes are made by combining two dough balls, rolling them thin, cooking them until done, then separating them. They are very thin, then steamed until soft, ready to be eaten with various fillings, making them very delicious.
There is an interesting legend about the custom of eating stir-fried beans or popcorn on the second day of the second lunar month. Once, the Jade Emperor punished humanity by ordering no rain for three years. The Jade Dragon, who controlled the天河 (Heavenly River), could not bear it and secretly brought rain, for which he was punished by the Jade Emperor, cast down from heaven and pressed under a big mountain. The Jade Emperor said: 'Unless golden beans bloom, you will never return to heaven.' People searched everywhere for blooming golden beans but couldn't find any. On the second day of the second lunar month the following year, people were drying corn seeds and suddenly noticed their golden color, just like golden beans. So, every household stir-fried beans and popped corn to offer to the Jade Emperor. The Jade Dragon shouted loudly to the Jade Emperor: 'The golden beans have bloomed! Let me out!' The Jade Emperor had no choice but to pardon the Jade Dragon. Since then, people have eaten stir-fried beans and popcorn on the second day of the second lunar month.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本封面，标题为《二月二的故事》，画面中一个女孩仰头接雨，面带微笑，背景有雨滴，下方标注出版社为连环画出版社。
[P2] 本页为绘本第2页，左侧是书名页，包含书名《二月二的故事》、改编者司南、绘画者杨景芝及出版社连环画出版社；右侧页面开始讲述故事，介绍黄河边的龙斧山、山上的龙王庙以及山下勤劳勇敢的小伙子强娃。
[P3] 本页左侧讲述强娃娶了采药姑娘莹花，两人十分幸福；右侧则描述当地已连续三年大旱，穷人们纷纷拜神求雨。
[P4] 强娃认为祈求老天爷无用，决定挖掘干涸的黑龙潭来寻水；他和妻子莹花已连续一个月挖掘，却一滴水也没挖出。
[P5] 强娃在二月初一继续挖掘干涸的黑龙潭，一镢头下去突然金光四射；与此同时，天上掉下一个石头蛋蛋，在他和妻子莹花脚边滚来滚去。
[P6] 石头蛋蛋突然变成一只白鸽，莹花想捉它时，白鸽扑棱棱飞走了；右侧画面是一位白发长须的老者，似乎在讲述或指点着什么。
[P7] 白鸽化作老公公，指点强娃和莹花去龙斧山寻水，随后化作青烟消失；强娃和莹花按指示翻山越岭，来到龙王庙。
[P8] 强娃和莹花来到龙王庙，看到铁架上放着一把看似千斤重的巨大斧头，强娃拿起斧头发现它异常轻便。
[P9] 强娃和莹花连夜赶回黑龙潭，强娃用劈山斧猛劈潭底硬盖，大地震动，一股清泉从黑龙潭中喷涌而出。
[P10] 泉水从黑龙潭喷涌而出，一条青龙从水中升起并腾空飞起，随后天降大雨，干旱的土地和枯萎的树木终于得到滋润。
[P11] 左侧画面描绘人们在大雨中欢庆，有人举碗接雨，有人跪地祈祷，周围摆放着陶罐；右侧画面中强娃与莹花被众人簇拥，怀抱白鸽，周围有人持鱼、持杖，场面热闹，象征干旱解除、生活富足。
[P12] 雨停后，人们感谢强娃和莹花，孩子们唱起“二月二，龙抬头”的歌谣，从此这一天被定为龙抬头的日子。右侧页面介绍了“二月二”节气的由来、天文含义及各地相关的传统习俗和禁忌。
[P13] 本页介绍了二月二的传统饮食习俗，如吃炒豆、春饼等，并讲述了一个关于玉龙被压山下、人们通过炒豆开花救出玉龙的传说，解释了吃炒豆和爆玉米花的由来。
